column4: I prefer Scenario 1, where different cultural groups maintain unique AI systems based on their own values. Every society, country, and group has its own history, beliefs, lifestyle, and ethical concepts. If AI operates within a single global framework, it may inadvertently eliminate cultural diversity, allowing certain values to dominate, while marginal cultures may be ignored or even erased. Scenario 1 allows different civilizations to retain their own wisdom and integrate it into AI to maintain cultural identity and autonomy. AI is not a simple computing tool, but a key technology that affects the operation of human society. If AI operates based on a unified ethical framework, it may not be able to effectively adapt to the complex needs of different societies. For example, Japan's concept of "harmony" is suitable for their collectivist culture, but may not be appropriate in countries that emphasize individual freedom. Adapting AI to local culture can better solve the real problems of each society. A unified AI system means that certain institutions, countries, or groups may control the direction of global AI development, and users around the world can only passively accept it. This centralized power may lead to technological monopoly, cultural hegemony, and even exacerbate global inequality. Scenario 1 allows different regions to build their own AI systems, thereby forming a more balanced global technology ecosystem.
